currentState: The Yeels progress bar only displays progress. It has no gesture of any kind. lib/features/reels/presentation/widgets/reel_progress_row.dart:24-100: `ReelProgressBar` is a `ValueListenableBuilder` -> `Semantics(container, label 'Playback position', value '{position} of {total}', excludeSemantics: true)` -> `ClipRRect(key 'reel-progress-bar')` -> `SizedBox(height: trackHeight)`. `trackHeight = 2` is at line 46. It has no onIncrease/onDecrease, so screen-reader users cannot seek either.

`ReelProgressTimes` (reel_progress_row.dart:106-145) and `ReelProgressRow` (:149-197) read the same `ValueListenable<Duration>`. The times are shown only when there is at least 160*textScale of width (:169-170).

The phone (immersive) stage places the bar in `_OverlayFooter` at reel_card.dart:2818-2823 (`PositionedDirectional(start 0, end 0, bottom 0, child: ReelProgressBar(...))`). It is the second child of the footer Stack, after the IgnorePointer scrim (:2794-2817). The identity block (:2836-2844) and the action rail (:2846-2866) are later siblings anchored at bottom `AppRhythm.item` = 12 (lib/core/theme/app_spacing.dart:40), or at bottom `AppRhythm.tight` = 8 for the horizontal rail, so they sit above the bar in z-order and overlap any hit band taller than about 8-12 px.

The card stage (>= 600 px wide, and the link destination) places the bar at reel_card.dart:1449-1452 inside `_StageFrameControls` (:1370-1459): `Padding(16,32,16,16)` -> Column [sound toggle/chip Wrap, 16 px gap, ReelProgressRow or ReelProgressBar]. `ReelOverlayMeasure` measures the height of that block at :1068-1080, and the frame composition insets depend on it, so changing its layout height would move the overlay geometry.

Tap-to-pause is `ReelPlaybackSurface` (reel_card.dart:2425-2458). It is an `AccessibleTapRegion(onTap: onToggle)` wrapped around the whole media, used by `_HostedReelVideoPlayer` (:2102-2118) and `_DefaultReelVideoPlayer` (:2381-2424). Double-tap-to-like is a `GestureDetector(onDoubleTap)` around the media only (:684-690). Both sit in the media subtree, which is a lower Stack sibling than the footer and frame controls (:865-908, :1060-1100). The comment at :1434-1436 says the overlay deliberately avoids opaque hit areas so the media tap still pauses.

Vertical feed swipe: `_FeedPager` uses `PageView.builder(scrollDirection: Axis.vertical)` (reels_feed_screen.dart:1477-1481). The reels feature has no horizontal drag recognizer and no `LogicalKeyboardKey` handling anywhere (grep of lib/features/reels).

The playback coordinator has no public seek. lib/features/reels/presentation/widgets/reel_playback_coordinator.dart public API: attachVideo (:257), detachVideo (:291), setActive (:344), autoplay (:368), setAutoplaySuspended (:390), setMuted (:399), toggle (:414), play (:440), pause (:450), synchronizeVideoTick (:461). Internally, `_pauseEngines(reset: true)` (:567-581) and `_loopVideo` (:583-605) seek only to the trim start.

Clock and trim math. The video position is the master clock. `position` is a separate `ValueNotifier` (:131-160), clamped to `timelineDuration`. For video, `timelineDuration` = trimEndMs - trimStartMs (:208-222). `_videoStart` and `_videoEnd` come from the composition trim (:224-230). The backing audio follows `_expectedAudioPosition` (:716-726): audioTrimStart + ((videoPos - videoStart) mod audioWindow).

`synchronizeVideoTick` (:461-501) publishes `video.position - _videoStart` on every controller tick, whether or not the video is playing. At `>= _videoEnd` while playing it loops (:478-487), and it drift-corrects the backing audio at most once every 750 ms when drift is over 180 ms (:488-500). `_playNow` (:503-557) reseeks the video to the trim start if the position is outside [start, end), and reseeks the audio to the expected position if it is off by more than 20 ms. So a paused video seek followed by play already realigns the backing audio.

Photo Yeels: the timeline is the backing-audio interval (:216-221). The audio engine is loaded lazily on first play (`_ensureAudio` :607-634, which also forces `_audioPosition = _audioStart`, so it would overwrite any pre-play seek). The end is enforced by `_photoEndTimer` (:696-708) and by `_onAudioPosition` (:636-651).

Autoplay gate (:368-387): `blocked = !autoplayEnabled || _disposed || !_active || _autoplaySuspended || _viewerPaused || _desiredPlaying || !canToggle`. A scrub that sets `_desiredPlaying = false` would let a concurrent autoplay() call start playback mid-drag, for example from attachVideo (:285) or setAutoplaySuspended(false) (:393).

Watch-time accounting: `onVideoProgress` counts only deltas where 0 < delta <= 1 s while playing (:470-477). ReelCard adds these up toward `recordViewed` after 3 s (reel_card.dart:404-407, wired at :428). Pausing for a scrub nulls `_lastViewedPosition` through `_setPlaying(false)` (:835-839), so a drag does not inflate views.

The real video driver is `_VideoPlayerPlayback.seek` -> `controller.seekTo` (reel_card.dart:2460-2484). The controller listener `_handlePlayback` calls `synchronizeVideoTick` on every value change, including after a seek (:2255-2276). Audio uses audioplayers `seek` (reel_playback_coordinator.dart:846-848).

Precedent in the same feature: `ReelDraftPreviewState.scrub` (lib/features/reels/presentation/widgets/reel_draft_preview.dart:463-488) already coalesces seeks during a drag, keeping one native seek in flight with the newest target winning, and pauses the coordinator first. It seeks the decoder directly, bypassing the coordinator.

ADR-209 (docs/Decisions.md:12866ff) defines the 2 px hairline. At :13245-13250 it records that the transparent `Slider` overlays and seek `GestureDetector`s stay in the callers and are not part of the waveform primitive. Nothing in ADR-209 forbids a hit band around the 2 px track.

Existing tests that pin the bar: test/reel_progress_row_test.dart (bar/label value, unknown timeline, photo bar), test/reels_phone_overlay_stack_test.dart:40-72 (`progress.bottom == frame.bottom`, and the progress rect must stay outside the clear-media band), test/reel_autoplay_test.dart:505-535 (sound rect bottom <= bar top), and test/reel_footer_bar_test.dart:143-152 (bar/times presence). They find the bar through `reelProgressBarKey` in test/reel_stage_test_support.dart:32. rootCause: This is a missing feature, not a regression. `ReelProgressBar` (reel_progress_row.dart:48-99) is a pure display: a 2 px `SizedBox` under a label/value-only `Semantics` with `excludeSemantics: true`. Its three call sites (reel_card.dart:1449-1452 and :2818-2823) attach no gesture. `ReelPlaybackCoordinator` has no public seek API (reel_playback_coordinator.dart:257-501), so there is nothing to scrub the video and the backing audio together. The only seeks are internal resets to the trim start. Even with a gesture, a 2 px target is far below the 48 px minimum.
design: 1. Coordinator seek API (reel_playback_coordinator.dart, additive, no behavior change when unused). New private state: `bool _scrubbing`, `bool _resumeAfterScrub`, `Duration? _scrubTarget`, `bool _scrubPumpQueued`, `Duration? _pendingPhotoOffset`. New getter `bool get isScrubbing` and getter `bool get canSeek => _active && timelineDuration > Duration.zero && (video Reel ? _video != null : _hasPlayableBackingAudio)`.

1a. `Future<void> beginScrub()`: no-op unless canSeek. Sets `_resumeAfterScrub = _desiredPlaying` (also true when `_loading` with `_desiredPlaying`), `_scrubbing = true`, `++_commandVersion`, `_desiredPlaying = false`, and cancels the photo end timer. Does not touch `_viewerPaused`: a scrub is not a hand-pause. Then `_notify()` and enqueue `_pauseEngines(reset: false)` plus `_setPlaying(false)`.

1b. `void scrubTo(Duration offset)`: clamps offset to [0, timelineDuration - 1 frame]. Use `timelineDuration - 40ms`, floored at 0, so a release at the very end never lands on `>= _videoEnd`: `synchronizeVideoTick` would loop there (:478) and `_playNow` would reseek to the start (:512). Calls `_publishPosition(offset)` immediately, so the preview time and bar follow the finger. Stores `_scrubTarget = offset`. If no pump is queued, enqueues one `_pumpScrub` through `_enqueue`. The pump loops while `_scrubTarget != null`: take the target, null it, then `await video.seek(_videoStart + target)`. This keeps one native seek in flight with the newest target winning, the same pattern as reel_draft_preview.dart:466-488. For a photo Reel with loaded audio the pump does `audio.seek(_audioStart + target)` and sets `_audioPosition`. Without loaded audio it stores `_pendingPhotoOffset`.

1c. `Future<void> endScrub()`: runs the final pump, then does one commit operation under a fresh command version. For video it awaits `video.seek(_videoStart + target)`; if the audio is loaded it awaits `audio.seek(_expectedAudioPosition(videoPos))` and sets `_audioPosition` (this respects the video trim, the audio trim and the audio-window modulo). It sets `_lastDriftCorrection = null`, `_lastViewedPosition = null` and `_scrubbing = false`, then calls `_notify()`. If `_resumeAfterScrub && _active && !_autoplaySuspended && !_disposed`, it sets `_desiredPlaying = true` and runs `_playNow(command)`, which also re-aligns the audio if drift is over 20 ms and reschedules the photo end timer. Otherwise it stays paused. Resuming when the video was playing matches iOS AVPlayerViewController, Android ExoPlayer/Media3 PlayerView, TikTok, Instagram and the web <video> controls, so it applies on every platform.

1d. `void cancelScrub()` clears the scrub state without resuming. Call it from `setActive(false)` (:348-356), `detachVideo` (:291), `setAutoplaySuspended(true)` (:390-395) and `dispose` (:776). A sheet, route or background that arrives mid-drag must win.

1e. Guards in existing code. Add `_scrubbing` to the `blocked` list in `autoplay()` (:370-377) so an attach or suspension release cannot start playback under the finger. In `synchronizeVideoTick` (:461-464), skip `_publishPosition` while `_scrubbing`; otherwise late controller ticks from older seek targets would snap the bar back and jitter it. In `_onAudioPosition` (:636-651), skip publishing and finishing while `_scrubbing`. In `_playNow` for a photo Reel, after `_ensureAudio`, apply `_pendingPhotoOffset` (seek the audio to `_audioStart + offset`, set `_audioPosition`, clear it) before `_validPhotoAudioPosition`. Today `_ensureAudio` forces `_audioStart` at :630-632.

1f. `Future<void> seekBy(Duration delta)` for accessibility and keyboard: a one-shot `beginScrub` + `scrubTo(position + delta)` + `endScrub`, which keeps the play state. Use a 5 s step, the same step as `MomentTransportControls` semantics (moment_transport_controls.dart:127-131).

2. New widget `ReelProgressScrubber` in lib/features/reels/presentation/widgets/reel_progress_row.dart (next to the bar, so one file owns the timeline visuals). Inputs: `position` (ValueListenable), `total`, an `onMedia` flag, and a small interface `ReelScrubTarget { bool get canSeek; bool get isScrubbing; Future<void> beginScrub(); void scrubTo(Duration); Future<void> endScrub(); Future<void> seekBy(Duration); }`, which `ReelPlaybackCoordinator` implements. The test fakes stay trivial.

2a. Gesture: `RawGestureDetector` with only a `HorizontalDragGestureRecognizer` (`dragStartBehavior: DragStartBehavior.down`, so the first preview lands where the finger went down) and `behavior: HitTestBehavior.translucent`. Translucent with no hit children returns false from hitTest, so the Stack keeps hit-testing lower siblings. Taps therefore still reach the identity block, the action rail, the sound pill and, underneath, `ReelPlaybackSurface`: tap-to-pause and double-tap-to-like are unchanged. A vertical swipe that starts on the band still scrolls the feed, because the PageView's VerticalDragGestureRecognizer wins the arena when the vertical slop is crossed first. Once the horizontal recognizer wins, the vertical one is rejected, so a scrub never turns the page. The fraction is `localDx / trackWidth`, mirrored when `Directionality` is RTL, because the fill is `AlignmentDirectional.centerStart` (:86-90). onStart calls beginScrub then scrubTo; onUpdate calls scrubTo; onEnd and onCancel call endScrub.

2b. Touch-only tap-to-seek is deliberately left out. A touch tap on the band would compete with the identity and rail tap recognizers in the arena, and would turn every tap-to-pause near the bottom into an accidental seek. Mouse and trackpad get click-to-seek through a `TapGestureRecognizer(supportedDevices: {mouse, trackpad})` on the band, with a hover cursor (`SystemMouseCursors.click`) and hover growth of the track. That matches desktop and web conventions for the card stage and the link destination.

2c. Hit geometry without moving any layout. Immersive: in `_OverlayFooter` (reel_card.dart:2818-2823), add the band as the LAST child of the footer Stack: `PositionedDirectional(start 0, end 0, bottom 0, height: 40)`. It is top-most in z-order, but translucent and drag-only, so the rail and identity taps inside those 40 px keep working. The visible 2 px `ReelProgressBar` stays exactly where it is, keeping key `reel-progress-bar`. The 40 px band is inside `scrimHeight` (>= 48, :600-606), so test/reels_phone_overlay_stack_test.dart clear-media checks stay valid. Card stage: add a `Positioned(left 0, right 0, bottom 0, height: 16 + 2 + 22)` band as the last child of the `_StageFrameControls` Stack (reel_card.dart:1432-1457). Map x with the 16 px horizontal padding subtracted. When `ReelProgressRow` shows times, map only over the bar's width, measured with a GlobalKey on the bar or a LayoutBuilder that exposes the bar rect. The Column is not touched, so `ReelOverlayMeasure` and `_frameControlsHeight` (:1068-1080) and every frame-geometry test keep their numbers. Give the band key `reel-progress-scrub`.

2d. Scrub feedback. While `isScrubbing`, the track grows from 2 px to 4 px and shows a 12 px thumb (white on media, `palette.audioAccent` fill). A floating time label '{position} / {total}' (tabular figures, `overlayTextShadows`) sits above the thumb and is clamped inside the frame; on the phone stage it is the only place time is shown. Video frame preview comes from the coalesced live seeks. Under `MediaQuery.disableAnimationsOf`, the growth and label are instant (use `AppMotion.resolve` for every duration) and there is no easing. Optionally fire one `HapticFeedback.selectionClick()` on start. The centred play glyph of `_DefaultReelVideoPlayer` (reel_card.dart:2405-2421) is suppressed while `playback.isScrubbing`, so the frame preview is not covered by a play icon the viewer did not ask for.

2e. Semantics and keyboard. Replace the bar's label/value container node (reel_progress_row.dart:62-77) with a single node on the scrubber: `Semantics(slider: true, label 'Playback position' / 'Pozycja odtwarzania', value, increasedValue, decreasedValue ('{position} of {total}' / '{position} z {total}'), onIncrease: () => seekBy(+5s), onDecrease: () => seekBy(-5s))`, with `excludeSemantics: true` over the visuals, so there is still one announcement per fact. Keep the plain label/value node when `!canSeek` (unknown timeline or detached decoder). Focus: wrap the band in `FocusableActionDetector` with ArrowLeft/ArrowRight -> seekBy(∓/±5s), mirrored in RTL, and draw a visible focus ring using the `palette.focus` 2 px edge that ADR-209 uses elsewhere. Space and Enter stay with `ReelPlaybackSurface`. Arrow keys are free: the feed has no key handling (grep).

2f. The stage passes the coordinator. `_OverlayFooter` and `_StageFrameControls` already receive `_playback.position` and `timelineDuration` (reel_card.dart:878-879, :1082-1083). Add a `scrub: _playback` parameter at both sites, and let ReelCard's `_onPlaybackChanged` (:559-561) rebuild on `isScrubbing` changes. Both surfaces are already listened to, so no new listener is needed.

3. Platform notes, not measured. `video_player` `seekTo` on iOS uses AVPlayer with zero tolerance (accurate, slower on long GOPs). Android ExoPlayer defaults to exact seeks. Web sets `currentTime`. Coalescing keeps at most one outstanding native seek per platform. Latency and frame-preview smoothness have to be measured on device (seek round-trip ms per drag event on iPhone, a mid-range Android and Chrome) before any smoothness claim. I have not measured anything.

4. Voice (Głos) recommendation. Do NOT reuse the Yeels band on the story viewer's segmented `_ProgressBars`. In the stories grammar they are chain navigation, one segment per Moment, and they sit next to the 72 px previous/next tap zones and the ArrowLeft/Right = previous/next keys. Close the real gaps with the Voice pattern that already exists. (a) moment_story_viewer.dart `_StoryStage`: put the same transparent `Slider` + `MergeSemantics('Playback position')` overlay used in moments_feed_view.dart:3183-3237 over the `StoryWaveform` (:1187-1190), wired to a new `_seek` that calls `_player.seek` and updates `_position`. Keep the 34 px horizontal padding so it stays clear of the 72 px edge zones' vertical strip only where they overlap: the Slider must be layered above the zones. (b) `MomentDetailPanel`: replace the tap-only `GestureDetector(onTapDown)` (moments_feed_view.dart:3684-3706) with the same Slider overlay, so drag and screen-reader adjust work there too. Audio-only players can keep seek-on-change (the existing feed-row behavior). Pausing during the drag is optional and should be decided per the Voice owner. It is the same user need, but a different control shape, so I do not recommend one shared widget across Yeels and Voice.

risks: Arena edge cases: a diagonal flick that starts on the band goes to whichever recognizer crosses its slop first. A user trying to swipe to the next Yeel from the very bottom may occasionally start a scrub. The 40 px band on a translucent layer keeps this rare. Verify on device, because widget tests cannot prove the feel.

Android system back-gesture insets (left and right edges) swallow drags that start within about 24-32 dp of the screen edge on the full-width immersive bar. A drag started further in can still reach 0:00 and the end. Optionally inset the band's start and end by `MediaQuery.systemGestureInsetsOf(context)`.

Seek latency and frame-preview smoothness vary a lot: iOS zero-tolerance seeks on long-GOP uploads, low-end Android, and web streams served without range support. Coalescing bounds the queue but not the per-seek latency. Measure on real devices before claiming smoothness. Nothing here was measured.

Web: `audioplayers` seek before the source is ready, and `video_player_web` seek on a not-yet-buffered range, can resolve late. The command-version guards must drop stale completions. There is a risk of the bar jumping if `_scrubbing` gating is missed on any publish path.

Coordinator concurrency: the new operations must go through `_enqueue` and must bump `_commandVersion`. Otherwise an in-flight `_playNow` from autoplay could resume under the finger. That is the main correctness risk, and tests 7 and 8 above cover it.
Backing audio for a video Reel is not previewed during the drag, because both engines are paused. On release it snaps to the aligned position. This is intended, but it should be stated in the ADR.
Watch-time integrity: a seek must never produce an eligible progress delta. Keep `_lastViewedPosition = null` on every seek path.

Visual verification is required per CLAUDE.md: immersive on the iOS Simulator and Android, card stage on web and desktop at 600/900/1200, text scale 2x, RTL, and dark/light. Until then the feature is UNVERIFIED visually.

rootCause: This is a feature gap, not a regression. Server text channels reuse the club message store, and that store was built text- and GIF-only. It has no reaction field, callable or UI, and no media pipeline. The server scene's message tile has no context-action entry point at all. design: Scope: V1 servers only. Every new callable runs `readChannelAccess` from functions/servers/authority.js, which enforces server state, member revision, banned status, channel status, access policy and the restricted grant. Legacy clubs (no serverSchemaVersion) are refused with failed-precondition because they are a retired surface.

PERMISSION DECISION (react): a caller may react if they have the channel's `read` capability AND role != 'guest' AND no active restriction (assertNotRestricted, so a communication mute blocks it) AND an active profile. This lets members react in announcements and rules channels even though they cannot post there. Do NOT add a `react` key to capabilitiesFor: grantMatches compares the key count exactly (authority.js:159-168), so a new key would invalidate every existing restricted-channel grant and lock people out of private channels.

PERMISSION DECISION (attach): a caller may attach media if they have the channel's `write` capability (so only moderators and above in announcements/rules; guests never), channel kind is text/announcements/rules, the email is verified (the Storage create rule requires isVerified), the caller is not restricted and the profile is active. This is the same authority as sendClubMessage.

PERMISSION DECISION (media read): a viewer gets bytes only through a callable that re-runs readChannelAccess(capability:'read'). A restricted grant is therefore enforced at every view, and a member who leaves, is banned or loses the grant cannot obtain a new URL; a URL already issued stays valid until its 90s expiry, the same residual SECURITY.md already accepts. Deleted messages never receive a grant.

PERMISSION DECISION (removal): moderators remove media messages through the existing moderateClubMessage, which keeps its rank-ordering and owner protection. Add a new author-only callable deleteServerChannelMessageV1, because V1 authors currently have no way to retract even a text message (firestore.rules:3898 is legacy-only), and posting a photo you cannot take back is a real problem.

Hot-document contention: every reaction is a transaction on the message doc. A popular announcement in a large community could see aborted or retried transactions. Acceptable at current scale. Grant latency and cost: each media bubble needs a signed URL. Without the batched access callable and a client cache, a thread of 250 messages could fire dozens of callables. Batch at most 20 ids, cache until expiry and render lazily as tiles become visible.

Bytes already fetched through an issued V4 URL stay valid for at most 90s after a ban or leave. This is the same accepted residual as SECURITY.md's private-media section and must be stated in the new SECURITY.md section.

currentState: Only Functions write `liveness` (via the Admin SDK). firestore.rules:1423-1425 `noClientChannelLiveness()` blocks any client write that carries a `liveness` key, so the rules never block a reset. A client write is not the cause.

`liveness` becomes true in exactly one place: `startServerChannelSessionV1` at functions/servers/sessions.js:117-120. The same transaction sets `activeSessionId` and `channelLiveness(now)` on the channel, and `isLive:true` plus `voiceSessionId` and `livekitRoomName` on the rooms/{anchor} doc (sessions.js:121-124).

`liveness` goes back to false in only these places. (1) `endServerChannelSessionV1` at sessions.js:258-263, which only the session starter or a member with `moderate` can call (sessions.js:245); the only client caller is the "End" confirm dialog, server_conversation_dock.dart:303-323 -> server_session_controller.dart:525-557. (2) `stageConvergenceSessionEnd` at convergence_lifecycle.js:106-137 (archive, delete, ownership transfer, moderation). (3) The ADR-180 stale sweep, session_staleness.js:83-163, which also uses (2). (4) A late-ACK fence in session_control.js:377-381 that only clears a projection whose `activeSessionId` is already null. (5) Creation and migration write the idle value: channels.js:281, documents.js:45, migration_apply.js:885.

Leaving never ends the generation, and the code says so: `ServerSessionController.leave()` (server_session_controller.dart:560-584) is documented as "the server, the channel and any live generation stay exactly as they are". It only disconnects the LiveKit link (server_media_connector.dart:672-724). No backend call is made on leave.

The server does not count participants. Token issuance explicitly does not track presence (sessions.js:212-213: "isOnline and the online/participant counters await a verified provider event adapter"), and per ADR-177 (docs/Decisions.md:10767) the projection carries no participant count.

The stale sweep is slow by design. It stages an end only when `max(startedAt, maxTokenExpiresAtMillis) + STALE_GENERATION_GRACE_MS` has passed (session_staleness.js:49, 60-62, 140). The grace equals the token TTL of 300 s (session_contract.js:7). It also needs `roomOccupancy` to report 0 or NOT_FOUND (session_livekit.js:315-328). It runs every 5 minutes (registration.js:886-895). ADR-180 (Decisions.md:10980-10982) states that the stale badge lasts "about 15 minutes" after the room empties: 5 min token TTL + 5 min grace + up to 5 min cadence.

The sweep only finds candidates through `rooms.where('isLive','==',true)` (session_staleness.js:132). A channel whose `liveness.isLive` is still true while its anchor room is not live (projection drift) would never be seen by any sweep. Nothing enumerates channels by `liveness.isLive`.

A verified LiveKit webhook exists: `receiveLiveKitAchievementWebhook`, functions/achievements/livekit_http.js:933-945, exported at functions/index.js:641. 1. Leaving a server channel only disconnects the local LiveKit link. See `ServerSessionController.leave()`, lib/features/servers/data/services/server_session_controller.dart:560-584, documented as leaving "any live generation ... exactly as they are".
2. The generation (`channelSessions` status `live`) and its public projection `channel.liveness {isLive:true, startedAt}` are only retired in three ways: an explicit host/moderator "End" (`endServerChannelSessionV1`, functions/servers/sessions.js:258-263), a convergence event (archive, delete, transfer), or the ADR-180 stale sweep.
3. The sweep only acts once every token the generation issued has expired and a further 300 s grace has passed (session_staleness.js:60-62, 140; token TTL 300 s, session_contract.js:7), and it runs every 5 minutes (registration.js:886-895). A channel therefore stays LIVE for roughly 5 to 15 minutes after it empties. ADR-180 records this as "about 15 minutes".
4. The one provider signal that could close it promptly is unused. LiveKit's `room_finished`, sent about 20 s after the last departure with the default departure timeout, is only consumed for achievements (livekit_http.js:763-817). Production logs also show that webhook has received no deliveries since its 2026-09-07 deploy, so it is most likely not registered in LiveKit Cloud.
5. There is also a latent second cause. The sweep only enumerates anchors with `rooms.isLive == true` (session_staleness.js:132), so a channel projection left `isLive:true` while its anchor is not live would stay LIVE forever. The sweep logs from 2026-09-16 to 2026-09-19 show `scanned:0` on every tick. If Kamil saw a LIVE badge lasting much longer than about 15 minutes, this drift is the explanation, and a read-only production query must confirm it before the backfill is sized.

design: 1. Extract one shared staging helper. In functions/servers/session_staleness.js, generalize `stageIfStillStale` into an exported `stageEmptyGeneration({anchor, observedMaxTokenExpiresAtMillis, reason, admissionCheck})`. It keeps the current transaction exactly: `canonicalServer` -> `readConvergenceBindings` -> session `live` + same `sessionId`/`roomId` -> `maxTokenExpiresAtMillis` unchanged -> `stageConvergenceSessionEnd` with the room and channel patches. Only the admission predicate becomes a parameter. The identity stays deterministic per generation and reason, e.g. `digest('server.session.empty.v1', binding)`. That keeps it one writer and one worker, with no second state machine.

2. Add an additive helper `recentAdmission(sessionRef, sinceMillis, excludeUid)`. It queries `channelSessions/{id}/tokenRecipients` (written at sessions.js:193-198; path at session_authority.js:19) with `where('lastIssuedAt','>', Timestamp.fromMillis(sinceMillis)).limit(2)`, served by the automatic single-field index. With `ADMISSION_WINDOW_MS = 30_000`, a person who was just issued a token and is still connecting blocks the end.

3. Last-leave path (server-authoritative). Add a callable `releaseServerChannelSessionIfEmptyV1({serverId, channelId, sessionId, requestId})` to the session service in functions/servers/sessions.js and register it in functions/servers/registration.js. It must be secret-bound (LIVEKIT secrets) and pass through the activation gate like the other callables.

3a. Authority for the callable: `readBoundSessionAccess(capability:'joinVoice')`. The caller must hold a `tokenRecipients` doc for this generation, which prevents a member who never joined from probing or ending someone's session. Replay goes through the `operations.execute` ledger.

3b. Outside a transaction, the callable calls a new adapter method `livekit.roomOccupancy({...binding})` extended to return participant identities, and counts participants excluding the caller's uid. The caller may not be removed yet after a clean disconnect. The count must be 0 or NOT_FOUND. A provider error or malformed answer means "occupied", so nothing changes.

3c. The callable then runs `recentAdmission(now-30s, excludeUid=caller)`, which must be empty, and then `stageEmptyGeneration` with `observedMaxTokenExpiresAtMillis`. A token minted concurrently moves the bound, so the commit is refused as `changed`.
3d. The callable returns `{outcome:'ended'|'occupied'|'changed'|'unknown'}` and never errors on 'occupied'.

3e. Client: in `ServerSessionController.leave()`, after `_cleanupLink(link)`, fire a best-effort `unawaited(_repository.releaseChannelSessionIfEmpty(...))`. Only do this when this generation was actually connected, and skip it when `endSession()` already ended it. Add the method to `ServerService`/`ServerRepository` next to `endChannelSession` (server_service.dart:572). Failures are swallowed; the webhook and sweep backstop it. A leave while the app is killed is covered by 4 and 5.

4. Provider path (fast backstop that needs no app update). In functions/achievements/livekit_http.js `handle()` (line 819), when `webhook.type === 'room_finished'` and `isServerRtcNamespace(webhook.roomName)`, also call a new staleness-service method `stageFinishedProviderRoom({livekitRoomName, finishedAtMs})`. This runs after the achievement close and isolated from it: a failure there must not turn the delivery into a 400/500 for achievements, and vice versa.

4a. `stageFinishedProviderRoom` resolves the binding with `resolveRtcBindingForLiveKitRoom` and requires the session to be `live`. It requires `recentAdmission(finishedAtMs - 30s)` to be empty, re-reads `roomOccupancy` (0 or NOT_FOUND), and then calls `stageEmptyGeneration`. It is gated on `activation.workersEnabled()`.
4b. Result: LIVE clears about 20 s after the room empties, even for crashed or killed clients.

4c. Needs Kamil: register `https://europe-west1-yovoice-ec54a.cloudfunctions.net/receiveLiveKitAchievementWebhook` as the webhook URL in the LiveKit Cloud project. It is signed with the same LIVEKIT_API_KEY the function already binds (livekit_http.js:55-56).

That makes the worst case one cadence (5 min) instead of about 15. Keep `maxInstances:1`.

It never uploads; the caller keeps its service, owner guards and outbox.

`YoMediaSendLimits { int maxImageBytes; int maxVideoBytes; Duration? maxVideoDuration; Duration minVideoDuration; int maxItems }`. Every call site passes its existing constants, so the limits do not diverge. Add additive public constants in message_service.dart: `directImageMaxBytes = 8 MB`, `directVideoMaxBytes = 64 MB`, `directVideoMaxSeconds = 60`, and replace the literals at 1709/1720/1786/1794/1805 with them, keeping the same values. Preview rendering. An image uses `Image.memory` of the bytes read once, which is bounded by the size check first, with BoxFit.contain on a palette.surfaceSunken stage, a semanticLabel, and an errorBuilder that shows a broken-image state with 'This photo can't be previewed'. A video uses a local `VideoPlayerController` built by a conditional-import factory `picked_media_video_controller{_io,_web,_stub}.dart` in lib/shared/widgets/media/ (io: .file(path); web: .networkUrl(blob)).
